items.text: ORDERED TO THIRD READING RULES CAL.162

items.actClause:
AN ACT to amend the agriculture and markets law and the general business law,
in relation to automobile tire inflation machines
items.lawCode: Amd §192, Ag & Mkts L; amd §396-x, Gen Bus L
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S4495

SPONSOR: MARTINEZ
 
TITLE OF BILL:  An act to amend the agriculture and markets law and
the general business law, in relation to automobile tire inflation
machines

 
PURPOSE OF THE BILL:  To ensure consistency in the regulation of tire
inflation machines mandated for service stations by providing exclusive
jurisdiction to the state through the Agriculture and Markets Depart-
ment.

 
SUMMARY OF SPECIFIC PROVISIONS:

Section 1 amends paragraph b of subdivision 6 of section 192 of the
Agriculture and Markets law to provide exclusive jurisdiction to the
state with respect to such section which requires service stations to
provide tire inflation machines. It specifically provides that a munici-
pality would not be restricted in enforcing the requirement of providing
functioning tire inflation equipment as required by the Commissioner of
Agriculture and Markets.

Section 2 amends subdivision 2 of section 396-X of the General Business
Law to provide exclusive jurisdiction to the state with respect to such
section which requires service stations to provide tire inflation
machines. It specifically provides that a municipality would not be
restricted in enforcing the requirement of providing functioning tire
inflation equipment as required by the Commissioner of Agriculture and
Markets.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

A motor fuel dealer is required to provide for an on premise motor driv-
en compressor capable of inflating automobile tires for use by customers
during the time the dealer is open for business. There are multiple
types of tire inflation machines which may be powered and operated
differently. Agriculture and Markets regulates weights and measures,
motor fuel pumps, octane and labeling requirements.  Motor fuel dealers
should be subject to a uniform regulatory regime.  Municipalities should
not be able to enact local laws which establish different requirements
for tire inflation equipment. As with other motor fuel related devices,
regulation should emanate exclusively from the Commissioner of Agricul-
ture and Markets. This bill eliminates confusion over the issue of
whether the state occupies the field and controls the regulation of tire
inflation machines for motor fuel dealers. At the same time this bill
makes it clear that a municipality is able to not enforce the provision
of a tire inflation machine by a dealer as required by the Commissioner
of Agriculture and Markets. There are in excess of 1500 local govern-
ments in New York State which could implement their own local laws on
tire inflation equipment. This bill makes it clear that any requirements
should be exclusively regulated by the state.

 
PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

None

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS FOR STATE AND LOCAL GOVERNMENTS:

None
 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
Immediately
